newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. firm to sell car insurance by mail in Japan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm to sell car insurance by mail in Japan.

text.p: U.S. insurer American Home Assurance Co, taking advantage of Japanese deregulation, announced plans on Friday for what it says will be Japan's first mail-order car insurance service.
The company, a unit of financial services giant American International Group Inc, said it would start selling car insurance policies through the mail in Japan in December.
The move comes at a time when Tokyo and Washington are locked in a dispute over further liberalisation of Japan's $400 billion a year insurance market.
Faced with fierce U.S. pressure to ease controls on its insurance market, Tokyo removed a ban on mail-order sales of auto insurance on October 11.
American Home Assurance would be the first firm to launch such a service in Japan.

Mail-order sales of insurance policies are expected to help foreign insurance companies, which have been trying to expand in Japan but lack an extensive network of sales agents, to drum up new business.
In 1982, American Home Assurance was the first company to launch mail-order sales of damage insurance policies in Japan.
The lingering dispute over insurance deregulation has become a major irritant in U.S.-Japan trade ties.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka are to meet on December 6-7 in Tokyo to make another push for a settlement, but doubts persist over whether they can do so by a December 15 deadline.

Washington accuses Tokyo of violating a 1994 bilateral pact by moving to deregulate a niche market for cover such as accident and nursing care policies before substantially opening its primary markets for life insurance and non-life cover.
U.S. firms have a strong foothold in the so-called "third sector" niche market.
